text:
carla: heads-up — product asked for a clear PRD for embedding dim changes + rerank compatibility by EOW. they want launch criteria and a rollback plan.

sanjay: ok. who from infra + product should we loop in? this has infra implications (replicas, storage)

maya: @product-ops pls confirm customer asks: is it just dimension increase (e.g., 512->768) or normalization behaviour change too?

product-ops: customer request A: allow higher-dim embeddings for enterprise tier. also they asked for stable similarity scores (no regressions). they want the ability to pin old vectors for 90 days.

carla: key constraints: 1) runtime supports mixed-dim vectors for rerank? 2) migration path without downtime 3) evaluation harness to detect semantic regression <= 2% on NLL/recall.

maya: propose PRD sections: background, scope, acceptance criteria, migration playbook, metrics + regressions, rollout plan, fallback policy.

tom: can we avoid storing two vector stores? storage cost will double. alternative: on-the-fly upscaling using PCA/projection? risky.

sanjay: infra note: runtime currently assumes fixed dim per model. supporting mixed-dim means adding a conversion layer in reranker pipeline or forcing reindex. both have perf tradeoffs.

maya: acceptance criteria suggestion:
- no-regen path: reranker must accept legacy vectors without blocking new queries
- quality: mean reciprocal rank (MRR) drop <= 1.5% on canonical eval set
- latency: p95 query increase <= 20ms on production baseline
- rollback: ability to switch routing to legacy model within 5 minutes

carla: +launch gating: automated eval job green, infra can serve new quant profiles, docs updated, and at least one customer pilot passed.

product-ops: pilot customers: AcmeCorp (high-volume), HealthSys (privacy constraints). need legal signoff for HealthSys.

tom: edge-case: batched requests with mixed dims — how to batch efficiently? current batching groups by model id only. possible approaches:
1) group by dim at request time (adds scheduling overhead)
2) pad/truncate vectors to max dim (cheap, but risks distortion)
3) convert older vectors to new dim during read (expensive but single-source)

sanjay: I'd prefer approach 3 for correctness during pilot, but we should measure CPU cost. fallback: pad+mark with metadata to avoid false positives.

maya: note about normalization: some customers store L2-normed vectors and expect cosine similarity. if dim changes we must preserve normalization semantics. acceptance must include tests that cosine similarity of migrated top-K remains within tolerance.

carla: can someone draft a minimal RFC with migration playbook and perf tests? include sample commands for rolling back. e.g.:
```
# snapshot current index
redwood index snapshot --name pre-dim-change-1794
# deploy rerank adapter in canary
kubectl apply -f rerank-adapter-canary.yaml
# switch traffic 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks
```

tom: I'll draft infra section (batch semantics + conversion microservice).

maya: I'll draft quality metrics + eval harness config (will include NDCG, MRR, recall@10 and a prompt set).

sanjay: I'll run perf baseline and estimate CPU/storage delta for approaches 2 vs 3.

product-ops: timeline: draft RFC by Thu, sync with legal for HealthSys by Fri, pilot ready next Wed. is that realistic?

carla: sounds tight but ok if we keep scope minimal. main ask: make PRD explicit about which litmus tests gate rollout.

deploy-bot: deployment queued — CI checks passed for branch dim-change/rerank-adapter (build #4521). :rocket:

maya: one more edge-case — rerank KD-tree / ANN index invariants. dimension change might require re-sharding of index partitions. call that out as high-risk.

carla: agreed. mark ANN reindex as 'must have' for full rollout, 'canary fallback' for pilot.

sanjay: i'll post a short perf summary tomorrow morning.

carla: great. next steps: tom + maya + sanjay to produce sections; carla to consolidate into RFC draft; product-ops to own pilot coordination. ping me with blockers. :thumbsup:
